review: Strengthening literature positioning and finite-power evidence with a model-based reference

formal_integrity.retired_expository_label: eq:scalar-C; scalar envelope now stated inline

literature.formatting_changes: Consistent conference venue abbreviations; removed redundant URLs where complete metadata/DOIs are retained.

mathematical_review: Model reference uses a chi-square lower quantile to upper-bound unknown isotropic noise variance.
The row norm bound and global residual Lipschitz assumption control the second moment by Minkowski and independence of the last disturbance.
A local tanh derivative lower bound and nonnegative coupled shift yield the stated expected-gain lower bound.
Matrix/noise confidence failures or matrix/validation failures are combined by a union bound; independence is not required between calibration events.
scope_limits: Model-based certification is cheapest in this deliberately short example; no superiority over all model-informed methods is claimed.
The finite-horizon envelope is tighter than the uniform block envelope in this short example.
The study evaluates the sequential mixture, not tightness of the fixed-sample sufficient allocation.
Global regularity, replicated resets and a robust margin remain assumptions; gain proportional to displacement remains a power condition.
The range-only lower bound applies to its stated information class.
